Seven offences on one page

93Exposure and abandonment of a child under 12
94Concealment of birth by secret disposal of body
95Hiring or engaging a child to commit an offence (new)
96Procuration of child
97Kidnapping a child under 10 to steal from its person
98–99Selling and buying a child for prostitution
Section 93

Exposure and abandonment of child under twelve

Elements

✓Father, mother or person having care of the child
✓Child under 12
✓Exposes or leaves it, intending wholly to abandon it
  • Up to 7 years, or fine, or both · if the child dies, trial for murder or culpable homicide is still open · old s.317
Section 94

Concealment of birth by secret disposal of dead body

1Child dies before, during or after birth
2Body secretly buried or disposed of
3Intent to conceal the birth → up to 2 years, or fine, or both · old s.318
Section 95

Hiring, employing or engaging a child to commit an offence

3 to 10 yearsand fine, for hiring, employing or engaging
Plusif the offence is committed: its punishment, as if he did it himself
Newno IPC equivalent
  • Covers using a child for sexual exploitation or pornography (Explanation)
Section 96

Procuration of child

1Induces a child to go from a place or do an act
2Intent or knowledge: forced or seduced to illicit intercourse with another
3Up to 10 years and fine
  • Old s.366A covered only a minor girl under 18; the Sanhita says “child”, so boys are covered
Section 97

Kidnapping or abducting child under ten to steal from its person

Under 10
Intentto take movable property dishonestly from its person
7 yearsand fine · old s.369
Section 98

Selling child for purposes of prostitution, etc.

1Sells, lets to hire or otherwise disposes of a child
2For prostitution, illicit intercourse or any unlawful and immoral purpose, at any age
3Up to 10 years and fine · old s.372
  • Female under 18 handed to a prostitute or brothel-keeper: the intent is presumed until the contrary is proved
Section 99

Buying child for purposes of prostitution, etc.

Buys, hires, obtainspossession of a child for the same purposes
7 to 14 yearsand fine; old s.373 had no minimum and capped at 10
  • The same presumption applies against a prostitute or brothel-keeper who obtains a female under 18
Selling · s.98Buying · s.99
Up to 10 years7 to 14 years
No minimumMinimum 7 years

Do not mix these up

Ages in this part: under 12 (s.93) · under 10 (s.97) · “child” under 18 everywhere else (s.2(3)).

S.95 is new: the hirer gets 3 to 10 years even if the offence is never committed.

S.94 is about hiding the birth, not about causing the death.
